mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 5.5% for two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a recession.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or GDP growth recovers quickly without equity impact.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in UNRATE above 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which raises wage pressures and input costs, ultimately leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as profit margins compress.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or inflation does not rise in response.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO of more than 0.5% for two consecutive months signals weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month and change < -0.5% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the decline in INDPRO reverses within one month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in HOUST and a fall in RSAFS (both > 2% month-over-month) signals a shift from inventory accumulation to depletion, which typically precedes a consumption-driven equity rally over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous month by >2% AND RSAFS < previous month by >2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the pattern fails during a recession.

mechanism_narrative: A positive co-movement between PAYEMS and UNRATE (both rising month-over-month) during a period of stable CPIAUCSL (< 0.2% monthly change) signals synchronized labor market strength without inflationary pressure, which historically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month AND UNRATE > previous month AND |CPIAUCSL - previous month| < 0.2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or inflation accelerates despite stable CPIAUCSL.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in FEDFUNDS below 2% during a period of rising GDPC1 signals a monetary policy easing in a growing economy, which typically boosts equity valuations over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or GDP growth slows sharply after the easing.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent monthly increase in GDPC1 for four consecutive months signals a robust demand recovery, which tends to drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or GDP growth reverts within the next month.
